payload.reason: The evidence provides multiple reasons why the beam search algorithm is considered inadequate, including issues with pruning, lack of diversity, and inefficiency in exploring the search space.

claims.text: Beam search prunes many paths that could yield high-quality outputs, wasting computational resources on less likely nodes.
Beam search does not effectively handle similar hypotheses, leading to inefficiencies in exploring the search space.
Increasing the beam size does not significantly improve diversity, and may decrease the quality of generated text.
The optimal model score achieved by beam search does not guarantee high-quality hypotheses, as the correlation between model score and output quality is weak.
